text:
Emily Zhao: We need to lock down the synthetic probes + network path health checks for the failover triggers. Key question: where do we run probes from so we don’t create our own false positives? (ISP blip, single AZ, etc)

Miles Thornton: +1. Last incident had a ton of noise from “packet loss” that turned out to be one transit path. If the trigger engine consumes this signal, we need it to be robust.

Victor Alvarez: Current options I see:
1) run probes *inside* each region (from the cluster nodes / daemonset)
2) run probes *outside* (edge POP / separate VM per region)
3) run from both and require quorum / majority

Victor Alvarez: False positives we’ve seen historically:
- probe host itself is unhealthy (CPU steal, conntrack, local DNS)
- single AZ network issue but region is fine
- path-specific issue (one ISP / one interconnect)
- ICMP blocked or deprioritized while TCP is fine

Irene Choi: For the failover upgrade, I’m strongly against ICMP-only. Can we define it as TCP/TLS handshake + optional HTTP GET to a lightweight endpoint?

Victor Alvarez: Yep. ICMP can be supplemental but not the primary. I’d do:
- TCP connect (443)
- TLS handshake (SNI set)
- HTTP GET /healthz (or /readyz) on a dedicated “probe responder” service
- record p50/p95/p99 connect+tls time and error types

Aisha Bello: From SLO/alerting side, I need the signal to be interpretable. “Packet loss 8%” with no context is hard to map to customer impact. If we can break out failure modes (dns, tcp, tls, http) that’d help.

Rafael Mendes: +1. Also, we should be careful about “probe says bad” when customer traffic is fine. Whatever we ship should start as monitor-only.

Harish Reddy: Where this matters: safe-to-failover checks also look at cross-region connectivity when we’re about to shift traffic. If probes are too noisy, we’ll either block legitimate failovers or trigger them too early.

Emily Zhao: Proposal: use 3 vantage points per region:
- 1 in-region (daemonset) per AZ (at least 2 AZs)
- 1 “neutral” VM in the same cloud region but separate project/account
- 1 from edge/POP (if we have it) or from a known stable external provider
Then aggregator does quorum logic: “region network impaired” only if >=2 distinct vantage groups agree.

Victor Alvarez: That’s reasonable but be careful with cost/ops. Daemonset is easy. Separate VM per region is fine. External provider adds vendor dependency.

Logan Wright: For publishing the signal: do we want raw probe series or a derived boolean + reason code? Trigger engine would prefer a stable contract.

Miles Thornton: Contract should include both, imo:
- derived state: OK | DEGRADED | FAIL
- reason: DNS_ERROR | TCP_TIMEOUT | TLS_FAIL | HTTP_5XX | HIGH_LATENCY
- supporting metrics (counts/latency) for dashboards/debug

Aisha Bello: Agree. If we only ship a boolean, it’ll be impossible to tune. But if we ship 20 raw metrics, it’ll be flappy.

Victor Alvarez: On “where to probe to”: should we probe:
- region -> region (cross-region paths)
- external -> region (ingress)
- region -> critical upstream deps (object store, auth, etc)

Emily Zhao: I think we need at least two:
A) external -> region ingress (captures what customers see)
B) region -> region (captures what fails during failover / reroute)
Region -> deps is good but might belong in dependency health rather than network health.

Irene Choi: +1. Keep “network path health” scoped. Otherwise every upstream brownout looks like a network incident and we fail over for the wrong reason.

Victor Alvarez: For external -> region, “external” must not be a single point. We should avoid probing from a single EC2 instance in us-east-1 and then declaring eu-west-1 down because us-east-1 had a transient.

Rafael Mendes: Can we do “external” as: 2 regions that are not the target region? Like probe eu-west-1 from us-east-1 + us-west-2.

Victor Alvarez: Yes, that’s better. Still cloud-internal though.

Emily Zhao: That’s okay for v1. We can add true outside later. Main goal is to avoid single vantage.

net-probe-bot: FYI last 30d probe incident summary (internal): false positives were primarily single-AZ probe hosts (41%) and DNS resolver timeouts (27%). Link: https://go.redwood.ai/net-probe-summary (internal)

Miles Thornton: DNS resolver timeouts: is that us? (node-local dns, or upstream)

Victor Alvarez: Mix. Some are node-local dns / conntrack exhaustion on probe nodes (self-inflicted), some are upstream resolver slowness. That’s why probe hosts must be isolated + monitored.

Irene Choi: If we run daemonset probes on data plane nodes, we *will* capture node-level issues and call it “region network degraded”. That’s not what we want.

Emily Zhao: So maybe split:
- in-region probes run on dedicated small “probe pool” nodes (tainted), not on inference hosts
- those nodes should exist across AZs

Harish Reddy: Dedicated probe pool capacity is easy (tiny). Just don’t put it on the critical GPU fleets.

Victor Alvarez: Also need to ensure probes don’t route over the same NAT / egress as customer traffic if we can help it; otherwise if NAT is broken, both are broken (maybe good), but if NAT is flaky only for probes, we’re dead.

Miles Thornton: Wait, do we expect probes to match customer path? Customer ingress is via edge -> LB -> service. If probes bypass edge, they’ll miss edge-specific issues.

Emily Zhao: Good point. For ingress probes, we should hit the same customer endpoint (edge URL) but from multiple regions. For internal region->region, we’ll use service mesh / internal endpoint.

Aisha Bello: Please don’t use “/healthz” on the main API if it’s cached and always green. We need something that exercises routing + minimal model path. Maybe a tiny “echo” route in the same stack.

Victor Alvarez: We can deploy a “probe responder” behind the same edge + routing layer. Minimal handler that returns 204 + headers indicating region/az.

Miles Thornton: That’s ideal. Also lets us detect “wrong region routing” (if we expected eu-west-1 and got us-east-1, that’s a signal too).

Rafael Mendes: For false positives: can we add a rule to ignore single vantage failures unless corroborated? i.e., quorum in aggregation layer.

Victor Alvarez: Yes. Suggested initial quorum:
- mark DEGRADED if >=2 vantage groups report elevated errors OR p95 latency > threshold
- mark FAIL if >=2 vantage groups report hard failures (tcp timeout / tls fail / http 5xx) for N out of M windows
We can tune N/M.

Aisha Bello: And add hysteresis. “Hold-down” so we don’t flap between OK/DEGRADED if a single window spikes.

Emily Zhao: Threshold starting point (draft):
- external->edge probe: error_rate > 2% over 5m OR p95 > 750ms over 5m => DEGRADED
- external->edge probe: error_rate > 10% over 5m => FAIL
- region->region: tcp/tls error_rate > 5% over 5m => DEGRADED
Numbers are placeholders.

Irene Choi: Those seem aggressive (750ms p95 could happen during benign congestion). Maybe use relative increase vs baseline per region.

Logan Wright: If we do relative baseline, we need a baseline store + seasonality. Might be hard for v1 but we can do “compare to last 24h median” as a simple baseline.

Victor Alvarez: Or keep absolute thresholds for trigger engine v1, but publish baseline/expected values for dashboards. Then we tune after game day.

Miles Thornton: +1. v1: avoid overfitting. Also, we need to explicitly handle “probe down” (no data). That shouldn’t immediately become FAIL.

Emily Zhao: Right. “No data” => UNKNOWN, and trigger engine should treat UNKNOWN as “don’t failover based solely on this signal”.

Rafael Mendes: That’s key for safety.

Victor Alvarez: Action items:
- Victor: draft probe spec (protocols, endpoints, reason codes) + quorum logic proposal
- Emily: propose deployment topology (probe pool nodes + cross-region sources)
- Logan: confirm metric names + publishing format to aggregator (derived state + raw counts)
We’ll review tomorrow.

Aisha Bello: Please include example metrics + how we map to alerts (burn rate vs immediate). I’ll plug it into the dashboards spec.

Harish Reddy: Also include “how many probes per region” + expected bandwidth. Capacity ops will want a heads up.

Victor Alvarez: Will do.

Irene Choi: One more: ensure probes run from at least 2 cloud accounts/projects so a single account-level networking policy issue doesn’t fake a region failure.

Emily Zhao: Noted. We can do “shared-services” project + “infra-probes” project.

Miles Thornton: Thanks all. This is exactly the kind of detail we were missing in the last incident.

net-probe-bot: Reminder: if you create a new probe endpoint, register it in service catalog for allowlists. See https://go.redwood.ai/svc-catalog (internal)
